title: 1628-drawdown-modulated-feedback-control-stock
universal_lens: A feedback control law I(k)=γ·M(k)·V(k) with modulator M(k)=(dmax−d(k))/(1−d(k)) enforces an almost-sure hard cap on percentage drawdown d(k) by driving position size to zero as d(k)→dmax. The gain γ* is calibrated via Monte Carlo to maximize expected log-growth under the constraint, trading ~12% terminal wealth for a 5% vs 22.5% drawdown cap.
gsi_mapping: The modulator M(k) acts as a conformal risk-control layer: given a predictive distribution over returns, it constructs a prediction set for stake size that guarantees coverage of the drawdown constraint. γ* becomes a calibration parameter learned via conformal quantile regression on historical pick returns, ensuring finite-sample validity of the drawdown cap.
gse_mapping: GSE implements a state-transition system where bankroll drawdown d(k) is the state variable. At each slate, the actuator scales posted stakes by M(k). When d(k)≥dmax, the system enters a forced-recovery regime (stakes=0) until d(k)<dmax. γ* is tuned offline via Monte Carlo on settled picks 2024–2026, then fixed online as a constant gain.

primitives.name: Drawdown Modulator M(k)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Investment rule I(k) = γ·M(k)·V(k), where V(k) is account value and M(k) = (dmax - d(k))/(1 - d(k)) is the drawdown modulator with d(k) the current percentage drawdown.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: dmax: dimensionless cap [0,1); d(k): dimensionless current drawdown [0,1); M(k): dimensionless scaling factor [0,1]
primitives.assumptions: d(k) < 1 (bankruptcy not yet occurred); dmax ∈ (0,1) preset; returns bounded so d(k) evolves continuously
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity at d(k)=1 (total ruin); modulator undefined. If d(k) ≥ dmax, M(k) ≤ 0 → position zero or negative (short), requiring floor at zero.

layer2.mapping: GSE slate-level stake scaler: each posted stake s_i ← s_i · M(k). The modulator is the actuator for the circuit-breaker levels calibrated in 1627/1629.
layer2.telemetry: Realized max drawdown per season; fraction of slates with M(k)<0.1; terminal wealth ratio vs unconstrained Kelly

primitives.name: Feedback Investment Rule I(k)
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Investment rule I(k) = γ·M(k)·V(k), where V(k) is account value and M(k) = (dmax - d(k))/(1 - d(k)) is the drawdown modulator with d(k) the current percentage drawdown.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: I(k): currency units (stake size); γ: dimensionless gain (Kelly-fraction multiplier); M(k): dimensionless modulator; V(k): currency units (account equity)
primitives.assumptions: γ constant (tuned offline); V(k) > 0; M(k) ∈ [0,1]; returns bounded in [Xmin, Xmax]
primitives.breakdown_regime: If γ·M(k) > 1, leverage > 100% → potential ruin in single step. If return distribution shifts (model risk), γ* becomes suboptimal or dangerous.

layer2.mapping: GSE core position-sizing kernel: total bankroll allocation = γ* · M(k) · bankroll. γ* ≈ 11.15 from TSLA Monte Carlo; GSE re-tunes on its own pick-return history.
layer2.telemetry: Expected log-growth per slate; Kelly fraction realized; leverage ratio I(k)/V(k)

primitives.name: Percentage Drawdown d(k)
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Assumptions: returns bounded (Xmin, Xmax known/estimated); the Monte Carlo return model matches future returns.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: V(k): currency units (current equity); max_{j≤k} V(j): currency units (running peak equity); d(k): dimensionless [0,1]
primitives.assumptions: Equity path V(j) observed without latency; peak computed over all prior steps j ≤ k
primitives.breakdown_regime: If V(k) = 0, d(k)=1 (ruin). If data feed stalls, peak may be stale → d(k) underestimated → modulator too large → oversized stakes.

layer2.mapping: GSE state variable for the drawdown governor. Computed each slate from settled bankroll. Feeds directly into M(k).
layer2.telemetry: Current d(k) vs dmax; time since last peak; frequency of d(k) > 0.5·dmax

primitives.name: Monte Carlo Gain Calibration γ*
primitives.verbatim_quote: The gain γ is tuned by Monte Carlo over the return distribution; the optimal γ*≈11.15 maximizes expected log-growth within the drawdown cap.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: γ: dimensionless; return distribution: empirical or parametric; T: horizon (steps); expectation over Monte Carlo paths
primitives.assumptions: Return distribution stationary and matches future; 100,000 paths sufficient; bounded returns (Xmin, Xmax known); dmax fixed
primitives.breakdown_regime: Non-stationarity (regime change) invalidates γ*. Small-sample model risk (60 returns in paper). Overfitting to historical path dependence.

layer2.mapping: GSE offline tuner: input = settled pick returns 2024–2026; output = γ* maximizing expected log-growth subject to dmax=0.20. Re-run quarterly.
layer2.telemetry: Out-of-sample log-growth vs in-sample; realized max drawdown vs dmax; γ* stability across re-tuning windows

reasoning_traces.think:
The drawdown-modulated feedback controller constructs a state-dependent gain M(k) that vanishes linearly as the current drawdown d(k) approaches the preset cap dmax. The investment rule I(k)=γ·M(k)·V(k) is a multiplicative policy: the Kelly fraction γ is attenuated by M(k)∈[0,1]. Since d(k)=1−V(k)/max_{j≤k}V(j), the modulator can be rewritten purely in terms of equity and its running maximum: M(k)=(dmax−1+V(k)/peak)/(V(k)/peak). As V(k)→peak·(1−dmax), M(k)→0, forcing I(k)→0 almost surely under bounded returns. The gain γ* is chosen by Monte Carlo to maximize 𝔼[log V_T] subject to the almost-sure constraint max_k d(k)≤dmax. This is a constrained stochastic control problem where the constraint is enforced by the feedback law itself, not by a Lagrange multiplier. The ~12% growth cost for dmax=0.05 vs unconstrained Kelly (dmax≈0.225) quantifies the price of the hard cap. Failure modes: (1) return distribution shift invalidates γ*; (2) discrete jumps can breach dmax before M(k) reacts; (3) small-sample model risk in γ* estimation; (4) latency in peak equity calculation.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: Rooted in Kelly (1956) growth-optimal betting and drawdown-constrained portfolio optimization (Grossman & Zhou 1993; Chekhlov et al. 2005). The feedback modulator M(k) is a discrete-time analog of the continuous-time risk-limiting controller in Browne (1999). The Monte Carlo gain tuning follows stochastic approximation (Robbins-Monro) and simulation-based optimization (Fu 2002). reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: The market is modeled as an adversarial return sequence bounded in [Xmin,Xmax] but otherwise unknown. The controller assumes the empirical distribution from 60 TSLA days is representative. An opposing agent (market regime shift) could exploit the fixed γ* by delivering returns outside the training support, causing M(k) to mis-scale. The Monte Carlo tuner assumes stationarity; a non-stationary adversary breaks the calibration.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: Veto conditions: (1) If realized max drawdown > dmax + ε (ε=0.01), halt trading — modulator failed. (2) If γ* changes >20% between quarterly re-tunings, flag model risk — distribution shift detected. (3) If peak equity stale >2 slates (data latency), freeze stakes — d(k) unreliable. (4) If I(k)/V(k) > 1.5·γ* (leverage spike), cut positions — modulator singularity near d(k)=1.
